items.title: 1.4.2 Properties of the Exponential Function (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 6-9: 1.4.2 properties (i)-(v) with side boxes, Example 7 (Figure 1.6), Example 8 (Figure 1.7)

blocks.text:
Is subtopic mein hum exponential function ki paanch properties ek ek kar ke saabit karenge. Har property graph ke baare mein ek pakki baat batati hai: graph kahan tak phaila hai, kahan kaat ta hai, oopar jata hai ya neeche, aur kis line ke qareeb jata hai. Aakhir mein in sab ko jor kar do graphs banayenge. Kitab ki tarah hum is function se shuru karte hain:
\[y = a^{x}\quad (a > 0,\ a \ne 1) \quad \text{...(1)}\]
(i) Domain, Continuity, Positivity and Range of Exponential Function

Domain: exponential function \(x\) ki har real value ke liye defined hai. \(x\) ki jagah koi bhi real number (positive, negative ya zero) rakh dein, expression \(a^{x}\) hamesha ek matlab rakhta hai. Is liye exponential function ka domain \(]-\infty, \infty[\) hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Notation ki baat: \(]-\infty, \infty[\) aur \((-\infty, \infty)\) ek hi cheez hain, yani tamam real numbers \(\mathbb{R}\). Ulta bracket \(]\ \ [\) ka matlab hai ke kinare wala number shamil nahin, bilkul gol bracket ki tarah. Yeh European tareeqa hai jo hamari kitab use karti hai, is liye dono pehchaniye.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Kya \(2^{x}\) mein \(x = -3\), \(x = 0\) ya \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) rakh sakte hain? Har ek ki value kya hai?
Jawab: haan, teeno allowed hain: \(2^{-3} = \frac{1}{8}\), \(2^{0} = 1\), \(2^{1/2} = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.414\). Koi bhi real number rakhein, jawab hamesha ek real number milta hai. Isi liye domain poora \(\mathbb{R}\) hai. Muqable mein \(\sqrt{x}\) ya \(\frac{1}{x}\) jaise functions mein kuch values mana hoti hain, magar \(a^{x}\) mein koi rok tok nahin.

Continuity: kisi point \(c \in\ ]-\infty, \infty[\) par continuity is equation se dikhayi jati hai:
\[\lim_{x \to c} a^{x} = a^{c}\]
Yeh dikhata hai ke exponential function apne poore domain \(]-\infty, \infty[\) par continuous hai. Yani exponential function ke graph mein koi chhalang (jump) ya surakh (hole) nahin.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: "Continuous" ka aasan matlab: graph ko qalam uthaye baghair banaya ja sake. Equation keh rahi hai ke jaise jaise \(x\) number \(c\) ke qareeb jata hai, \(a^{x}\) bhi asal value \(a^{c}\) ke qareeb jata hai. Maslan \(x \to 2\) ho to \(2^{x} \to 2^{2} = 4\); beech mein koi achanak chhalang nahin. Jaise seedhi ki bajaye dhalwan raasta: har qadam par aap thora sa hi oopar jate hain.

Positivity: agar \(x = n\) koi positive integer ho, to \(a^{n} = a \cdot a \cdot \ldots \cdot a\) (\(n\) dafa). Kyun ke \(a > 0\), aur positive numbers ka product positive hota hai, is liye \(a^{n} > 0\). Saath hi
\[a^{-n} = \dfrac{1}{a^{n}}\]
Kyun ke \(a^{n} > 0\), is ka reciprocal bhi positive hai, yani \(a^{-n} > 0\). Aur \(a^{0} = 1 > 0\).

Agar \(x\) rational ho, to \(x = \frac{p}{q}\), jahan \(p\) integer aur \(q\) natural number hai. To:
\[a^{x} = a^{p/q} = \sqrt[q]{a^{p}}\]
Integer wale case se \(a^{p} > 0\). Aur kyun ke positive number ka \(q^{\text{th}}\) root bhi positive hota hai, is liye \(a^{p/q} > 0\).

Is tarah har rational \(x\) ke liye \(a^{x} > 0\). Irrational \(x\) (jaise \(\sqrt{2}\) ya \(\pi\)) ke liye hum maan lete hain ke \(a^{x}\) bhi positive hai; is ka pakka saboot is level se aage ki baat hai.
Natija: har real number \(x\) ke liye \(y = a^{x} > 0\). Is ka matlab hai ke exponential function ka graph hamesha \(x\)-axis ke oopar rehta hai, kabhi neeche nahin jata.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text: Teeno cases numbers se aazmaiye: \(2^{3} = 8 > 0\); \(2^{-3} = \frac{1}{8} > 0\); \(8^{2/3} = \sqrt[3]{8^{2}} = \sqrt[3]{64} = 4 > 0\). Yahan tak ke \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{-5} = 32\) bhi positive hai. Negative power value ko chhota ya bara kar deti hai, magar negative kabhi nahin karti. Jaise kisi cheez ko baar baar aadha karte jayein, woh chhoti hoti jayegi, magar "minus" mein kabhi nahin jayegi.

Ab tak humne dekha ke graph kahan tak phaila hai (domain), toota hua nahin (continuity) aur hamesha \(x\)-axis ke oopar hai (positivity). Ab aakhri sawal: \(y\) ki kaun kaun si values milti hain? Yani range kya hai? Iske liye kitab chaar facts ikatthe karti hai.
Range: in facts ko dekh kar:

items: \(0 < a < 1\) ho to \(\lim_{x \to -\infty} a^{x} = \infty\) aur \(\lim_{x \to \infty} a^{x} = 0^{+}\).

blocks.text: Hum is natije par pohanchte hain ke exponential function (1) ki range \(]0, \infty[\) hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yeh chaar facts mil kar poori \(]0, \infty[\) kaise dete hain? Values 0 ke jitna chahein qareeb aa jati hain (fact 1 ya 2), jitna chahein bari bhi ho jati hain, aur graph mein koi gap nahin (fact 3). To beech ka har positive number kahin na kahin zaroor aata hai. Fact 4 batata hai ke 0 ya negative value kabhi nahin aati. Nishan \(0^{+}\) ka matlab hai "oopar se, positive values ke zariye, 0 ki taraf jana".
(ii) Intercepts of Exponential Function

\(y\)-intercept: \(y\)-intercept nikalne ke liye equation (1) mein \(x = 0\) rakhiye:
\[y = a^{0} = 1\]
Yani exponential function \(y = a^{x}\) \(y\)-axis ko point \((0, 1)\) par kaat ta hai.

\(x\)-intercept: \(x\)-intercept nikalne ke liye equation (1) mein \(y = 0\) rakhiye:
\[a^{x} = 0\]
Lekin har real \(x\) ke liye \(a^{x} > 0\). Is liye koi \(x\)-intercept nahin.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Matlab har exponential graph, base chahe kuch bhi ho, ek hi point \((0, 1)\) se guzarta hai: \(2^{0} = e^{0} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{0} = 1\). Kisi bhi exponential graph mein sab se pehle yahi point lagaiye; yeh muft ka point hai!

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(y = 5^{x}\) aur \(y = (0.3)^{x}\) \(y\)-axis ko kahan kaatte hain? Kya in mein se koi \(x\)-axis ko kaat ta hai?
Jawab: dono \((0, 1)\) par, kyun ke \(5^{0} = (0.3)^{0} = 1\). Aur koi bhi \(x\)-axis ko nahin kaat ta, kyun ke positive number ki koi bhi power zero nahin ban sakti. Agla box ek nayi istilah (term) samjhata hai jo property (iii) mein chahiye: strictly increasing aur strictly decreasing.

blocks.title: Strictly Increasing and Strictly Decreasing Functions
blocks.text:
Maan lijiye \(y = f(x)\) ek real-valued function hai aur \(x_{1}, x_{2} \in D_{f}\) koi do points hain jin mein \(x_{1} < x_{2}\). To function \(f\) kehlata hai:
(i) Strictly increasing agar \(f(x_{1}) < f(x_{2})\). Is surat mein \(x\) jab \(x\)-axis par baayen se daayen chalta hai to graph oopar uthta hai.
(ii) Strictly decreasing agar \(f(x_{1}) > f(x_{2})\). Is surat mein \(x\) baayen se daayen chalta hai to graph neeche girta hai.
Misaal: function \(y = x^{2}\) \(]-\infty, 0[\) par strictly decreasing aur \(]0, \infty[\) par strictly increasing hai.
(iii) Exponential Function is Strictly Increasing or Strictly Decreasing
Maan lijiye \(f(x) = a^{x}\), jahan \(a > 0\) aur \(a \ne 1\). Hum do cases alag alag dekhenge, kyun ke base 1 se bara ho ya chhota, rawayya ulat jata hai.
Case-1: If a > 1

Maan lijiye \(x_{1} < x_{2} \Rightarrow x_{2} - x_{1} > 0\). To
\[a^{x_{2}} = a^{x_{1}} \cdot a^{x_{2} - x_{1}}\]
Kyun ke \(x_{2} - x_{1} > 0\) aur \(a > 1\), is liye \(a^{x_{2} - x_{1}} > 1\). To:
\[a^{x_{2}} = a^{x_{1}} \cdot a^{x_{2} - x_{1}}\]
\[\Rightarrow a^{x_{2}} > a^{x_{1}}\]
Yani \(x_{1} < x_{2} \Rightarrow a^{x_{1}} < a^{x_{2}}\).
Is liye \(a > 1\) ho to \(y = a^{x}\) strictly increasing hai.
Case-2: If 0 < a < 1

Maan lijiye \(x_{1} < x_{2} \Rightarrow x_{2} - x_{1} > 0\). To
\[a^{x_{2}} = a^{x_{1}} \cdot a^{x_{2} - x_{1}}\]
Kyun ke \(0 < a < 1\) aur \(x_{2} - x_{1} > 0\), is liye \(a^{x_{2} - x_{1}} < 1\). To:
\[a^{x_{2}} = a^{x_{1}} \cdot a^{x_{2} - x_{1}}\]
\[\Rightarrow a^{x_{2}} < a^{x_{1}}\]
Yani \(x_{1} < x_{2} \Rightarrow a^{x_{1}} > a^{x_{2}}\).
Is liye \(0 < a < 1\) ho to \(y = a^{x}\) strictly decreasing hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is saboot ke peeche sirf do baatein hain:
1. Indices ka qanoon \(a^{m} \cdot a^{n} = a^{m+n}\), jis se \(a^{x_{1}} \cdot a^{x_{2} - x_{1}} = a^{x_{2}}\) banta hai. Yani \(a^{x_{2}}\) ko do tukron mein toda gaya.
2. 1 se bare base ki positive power 1 se bari hoti hai (\(2^{0.5} \approx 1.414\)); 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan wale base ki positive power 1 se chhoti hoti hai (\(0.5^{0.5} \approx 0.707\)).
Ab positive number \(a^{x_{1}}\) ko 1 se bari cheez se zarb dein to woh bara ho jata hai; 1 se chhoti cheez se zarb dein to chhota. Bas, yahi poora saboot hai. Jaise apni tankhwah ko 1.1 se zarb karein to barhti hai, 0.9 se karein to ghatti hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Bina calculator ke batayein: \(3^{1.5}\) bara hai ya \(3^{1.2}\)? Aur \((0.5)^{1.5}\) bara hai ya \((0.5)^{1.2}\)?
Jawab: base 3 > 1, to function increasing hai, is liye bari power bari value: \(3^{1.5} > 3^{1.2}\). Base 0.5 < 1, to function decreasing hai, is liye bari power chhoti value: \((0.5)^{1.5} < (0.5)^{1.2}\). Dekha, property (iii) ne hisaab ke baghair jawab de diya. Exam mein "compare karo" wale sawal isi tarah hal hote hain.
(iv) Injectivity of Exponential Functions

Ab chauthi property. Injectivity ka sawal yeh hai: kya do alag inputs kabhi ek hi output de sakte hain? Misaal ke taur par har student ka roll number alag hota hai; agar do students ka roll number same ho jaye to gadbad ho jati hai. One-to-one function mein har output ka "roll number" alag hota hai. Pehle kitab ka side box parhiye, phir saboot dekhte hain.

blocks.title: Definition of Injectivity (One-to-One Function)
blocks.text:
Yaad kijiye ke function \(y = f(x)\) injective (one-to-one) kehlata hai agar mukhtalif inputs hamesha mukhtalif outputs dein. Rasmi taur par function one-to-one hai agar: jab bhi \(x_{1}, x_{2} \in \operatorname{Dom} f\) ke liye \(f(x_{1}) = f(x_{2})\) ho, to \(x_{1} = x_{2}\) ho.
Function injective hai agar har horizontal line us ke graph ko zyada se zyada ek dafa mile; doosre lafzon mein, us ka graph strictly increasing ya strictly decreasing ho.

Maan lijiye \(f(x) = a^{x}\), jahan \(a > 0\) aur \(a \ne 1\). Aur maan lijiye kisi \(x_{1}, x_{2} \in\ ]-\infty, \infty[\) ke liye \(f(x_{1}) = f(x_{2})\). To:
\[a^{x_{1}} = a^{x_{2}}\]
Ab hum dikhayenge ke \(x_{1}\) aur \(x_{2}\) alag ho hi nahin sakte. Is tareeqe ko "contradiction" (tazaad) se saboot kehte hain: alag maan kar dekho ke ghalat baat nikalti hai.

Case-1: agar \(x_{1} < x_{2}\), to function \(f(x) = a^{x}\) se ya to \(a^{x_{1}} < a^{x_{2}}\) (jab \(a > 1\)) ya \(a^{x_{1}} > a^{x_{2}}\) (jab \(0 < a < 1\)). Dono surton mein yeh \(a^{x_{1}} = a^{x_{2}}\) ke khilaf hai, yani na-mumkin.
Case-2: agar \(x_{1} > x_{2}\), to function \(f(x) = a^{x}\) se ya to \(a^{x_{1}} > a^{x_{2}}\) (jab \(a > 1\)) ya \(a^{x_{1}} < a^{x_{2}}\) (jab \(0 < a < 1\)). Yeh bhi na-mumkin.
Is liye lazmi \(x_{1} = x_{2}\), aur natija yeh ke \(f(x) = a^{x}\) injective hai. Yani koi bhi horizontal line \(f(x) = a^{x}\) ke graph ko zyada se zyada ek dafa milti hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
\(y = x^{2}\) se muqabla kijiye: \(2^{2} = (-2)^{2} = 4\). Do mukhtalif inputs, ek hi output, is liye \(x^{2}\) one-to-one nahin (line \(y = 4\) us ke graph ko do jagah milti hai). Lekin \(2^{x} = 4\) sirf \(x = 2\) par hota hai.
Yahi injectivity exponential equations hal karne ki chaabi hai: \(2^{x} = 8 = 2^{3} \Rightarrow x = 3\). Base same ho to powers barabar kar do. Yeh 1.10 mein bohat kaam aayega.
(v) Horizontal Asymptote of Exponential Function

Dekhiye: agar \(a > 1\) ho to \(x \to -\infty\) par \(a^{x} \to 0^{+}\), aur agar \(0 < a < 1\) ho to \(x \to \infty\) par \(a^{x} \to 0^{+}\). Is se nikalta hai ke horizontal line \(y = 0\) exponential function ka horizontal asymptote hai.

blocks.title: Note: (Horizontal Asymptote)
blocks.text:
Horizontal asymptote ek horizontal line \(y = c\) hai jis ki taraf function us waqt jata hai jab \(x\) bohat bara (ya bohat chhota) ho, magar zaroori nahin ke graph use chhooye ya kaate.
Rasmi taur par horizontal line \(y = c\) function \(y = f(x)\) ka horizontal asymptote kehlati hai agar \(x \to -\infty\) ya \(x \to \infty\) par \(f(x) \to c\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab is note mein "Formally the vertical line \(y = c\) is called horizontal asymptote" likhti hai. Line \(y = c\) hamesha horizontal (leti hui) hoti hai, vertical (khari) nahin. Sahi baat: horizontal line \(y = c\) function \(y = f(x)\) ka horizontal asymptote hai agar \(x \to -\infty\) ya \(x \to \infty\) par \(f(x) \to c\). Upar hum ne sahi likha hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text: Numbers se dekhiye: \(2^{-10} = \frac{1}{1024} \approx 0.001\) aur \(2^{-20} \approx 0.000001\). \(2^{x}\) ka graph baayen taraf \(x\)-axis ke qareeb se qareeb tar hota jata hai, lekin \(2^{x}\) kabhi 0 nahin hota, is liye axis tak kabhi pohanchta nahin. Bilkul aise jaise aap har din deewar tak baqi faasle ka aadha chalein: har din qareeb, magar deewar ko kabhi na chhoo payein. Yahi asymptote hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(y = \left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{x}\) ka graph kis taraf \(x\)-axis ke qareeb jayega, baayen ya daayen? Aur \(y = 10^{x}\) ka?
Jawab: \(\frac{1}{4} < 1\), to \(x \to \infty\) par value 0 ki taraf jati hai, yani daayen taraf. \(10 > 1\), to \(x \to -\infty\) par value 0 ki taraf jati hai, yani baayen taraf. Dono ka asymptote ek hi line \(y = 0\) hai; sirf jhukao ki taraf alag hai.
Ab in tamam properties ko istemal kar ke kitab ki do misalon mein graphs banate hain. Ghaur kijiye ke hum ne pehle properties likhi hain aur phir sirf chand values; points ka dher nahin lagaya.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Example 7 mein hum wahi plan follow karenge jo 1.4.1 mein bataya tha. Yaad rahe ke kitab properties bullets mein likhti hai aur values do tables mein deti hai; hum ne in ko steps mein tarteeb se likha hai taa ke har qadam ki wajah saaf ho. Table mein \(x = 10\) aur \(x = 100\) jaisi bari values sirf yeh dikhane ke liye hain ke function kitni tezi se barhta ya ghatta hai; graph par plot karne ke liye sirf \(x = -2\) se \(2\) tak ki values kaafi hain.

blocks.title: Example 7
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = e^{x}\), ek exponential function jis ka base \(a = e \approx 2.718\) hai.
Maloom karna: is ka graph.
Tareeqa: sab se pehle hum woh properties lagayenge jo upar \(y = a^{x}\) ke liye saabit hui hain (domain, range, intercept, asymptote, increasing ya decreasing). Phir values ka chhota sa table, aur aakhir mein points ko hamwar curve se jorna. Kyun ke \(e > 1\), is liye \(a > 1\) wala case lagega.

Step 1: Domain aur range
\[\text{Domain} = \mathbb{R} = (-\infty, \infty)\]
\[\text{Range} = (0, \infty)\]
Kyun: \(a^{x}\) har real \(x\) ke liye defined hai aur hamesha positive hai, aur property (i) ke mutabiq range \(]0, \infty[\) hai. Yani graph poori \(x\)-axis ke oopar phaila hoga, magar \(y\) kabhi 0 ya negative nahin hoga.

Step 2: Intercepts
\[x = 0:\quad e^{0} = 1\]
Graph \(y\)-axis ko \((0, 1)\) par kaat ta hai; \(x\)-intercept koi nahin.
Kyun: har exponential function \((0, 1)\) se guzarta hai, aur \(e^{x} = 0\) ka koi hal nahin kyun ke \(e^{x} > 0\) (property (ii)). Yeh hamara pehla pakka point hai.

Step 3: Asymptote aur monotonicity
\(y = 0\) horizontal asymptote hai, aur \(f\) continuous aur strictly increasing hai.
Kyun: \(e > 1\), is liye \(x \to -\infty\) par \(e^{x} \to 0^{+}\) (property (v)), aur \(e^{x}\) baayen se daayen oopar chadhta hai (property (iii), Case-1). Matlab baayen taraf curve \(x\)-axis se lipat ta jayega aur daayen taraf tezi se oopar jayega.

Step 4: Positive \(x\) ki values
\[e^{1} \approx 2.718,\quad e^{2} \approx 7.389\]
\[e^{3} \approx 20.086,\quad e^{10} \approx 22026.466\]
\[e^{100} \approx 2.688 \times 10^{43}\]
Kyun: yeh values dikhati hain ke \(e^{x}\) kitni tezi se barhta hai; \(x = 10\) par hi value 22 hazaar se oopar hai! \(x \to +\infty\) par \(e^{x} \to +\infty\).

Step 5: Negative \(x\) ki values
\[e^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{e} \approx 0.368\]
\[e^{-2} \approx 0.135,\quad e^{-3} \approx 0.0498\]
\[e^{-10} \approx 0.0000454\]
\[e^{-100} \approx 3.720 \times 10^{-44}\]
Kyun: \(e^{-x} = \frac{1}{e^{x}}\), yani har value Step 4 ki kisi value ka ulta (reciprocal) hai. Is liye yeh positive hain, chhoti hain, aur \(x \to -\infty\) par 0 ki taraf jati hain, magar kabhi 0 nahin hoti.
Dhyan dein: calculator ki value ko round kijiye, kaatiye nahin: \(0.36788 \approx 0.368\).

Step 6: Plot kar ke jorna
Points \((-2, 0.14)\), \((-1, 0.37)\), \((0, 1)\), \((1, 2.72)\), \((2, 7.39)\) plot kijiye aur unhein ek hamwar, oopar chadhti curve se jodiye jo baayen taraf \(x\)-axis ke qareeb rahe magar use na chhooye (Figure 1.6).
Kyun: plotting ke liye values do decimal tak round ki gayi hain; curve ki shakal Steps 1-3 se tay hai.

Tasdeeq: ek value aur us ka reciprocal zarb ho kar 1 dene chahiyein:
\[e^{1} \times e^{-1} \approx 2.718 \times 0.368\]
\[\approx 1.000\]
Saath hi table ki har value positive hai aur \(x\) barhne se value barhti hai, bilkul jaise Steps 1 aur 3 ne bataya tha.
blocks.answer: \(f(x) = e^{x}\) ka graph woh hamwar, oopar chadhti curve hai jo \((-2, 0.14)\), \((-1, 0.37)\), \((0, 1)\), \((1, 2.72)\), \((2, 7.39)\) se guzarti hai; yeh \(x\)-axis ke oopar rehti hai aur \(y = 0\) is ka horizontal asymptote hai (Figure 1.6).

blocks.text: Upar ke tamam key points ke saath \(f(x) = e^{x}\) ka graph Figure 1.6 mein dikhaya gaya hai.

To the left it comes very close to the x-axis without touching it; arrows at both ends show that it goes on.

blocks.text: Note kijiye ke tamam exponential functions \(f(x) = a^{x}\), \(a \in \mathbb{R}\) aur \(a > 1\), ke graphs taqreeban Figure 1.6 jaise hi hote hain. Base jitna bara, curve daayen taraf utni hi tezi se oopar jati hai, magar shakal wahi rehti hai aur \((0, 1)\) wahi.

Ab doosri misaal. Is mein base 1 se chhota hai, is liye tamam properties wahi rahengi siwaye do ke: graph chadhne ki bajaye utrega, aur asymptote ki taraf jhukao baayen ki bajaye daayen hoga. Misaal shuru karne se pehle khud andaza lagaiye ke graph kaisa dikhega, phir hamare steps se milaiye. Yeh aadat exam mein bohat kaam aati hai, kyun ke ghalat graph foran pakra jata hai.

blocks.title: Example 8
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{x}\), ek exponential function jis ka base \(a = \frac{1}{2}\) hai.
Maloom karna: is ka graph.
Tareeqa: wahi plan jo Example 7 mein tha, bas ab \(0 < a < 1\) hai, is liye decreasing wala case lagega. Dekhte hain ke kya badalta hai aur kya wahi rehta hai.

Step 1: Domain aur range
\[\text{Domain} = \mathbb{R} = (-\infty, \infty)\]
\[\text{Range} = (0, \infty)\]
Kyun: yeh har exponential function \(a^{x}\) ke liye sach hai (property (i)), chahe base bara ho ya chhota. Yahan kuch nahin badla.

Step 2: Intercept
\[x = 0:\quad \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{0} = 1\]
Graph \(y\)-axis ko \((0, 1)\) par kaat ta hai; \(x\)-intercept koi nahin.
Kyun: property (ii); \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{x} > 0\) har \(x\) ke liye. Phir wahi pakka point \((0, 1)\).

Step 3: Asymptote aur monotonicity
\(y = 0\) horizontal asymptote hai; \(f\) continuous aur strictly decreasing hai kyun ke \(a = \frac{1}{2} < 1\).
Kyun: \(0 < a < 1\) ke liye \(x \to \infty\) par \(a^{x} \to 0^{+}\) (property (v)), aur property (iii), Case-2. Yahan farq aaya: ab curve daayen taraf \(x\)-axis se lipte gi aur baayen taraf oopar jayegi.

Step 4: Positive \(x\) ki values
\[\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{1} = 0.5,\quad \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{2} = 0.25\]
\[\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{3} = 0.125\]
\[\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{10} = \dfrac{1}{1024} \approx 0.0009766\]
\[\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{100} \approx 7.89 \times 10^{-31}\]
Kyun: \(x\) mein har 1 ke izafe se value aadhi ho jati hai; \(x \to +\infty\) par value 0 ki taraf jati hai.

Step 5: Negative \(x\) ki values
\[\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{-x} = 2^{x}\]
\[\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{-1} = 2,\quad \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{-2} = 4\]
\[\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{-3} = 8,\quad \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{-10} = 1024\]
\[\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{-100} = 2^{100} \approx 1.268 \times 10^{30}\]
Kyun: negative power \(\frac{1}{2}\) ko ulat kar 2 bana deti hai; \(x \to -\infty\) par value \(\infty\) ki taraf jati hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{-1}\) ka jawab \(-\frac{1}{2}\) nahin balke 2 hai.

Step 6: Plot kar ke jorna
Points \((-2, 4)\), \((-1, 2)\), \((0, 1)\), \((1, 0.5)\), \((2, 0.25)\) plot kijiye aur unhein hamwar, neeche utarti curve se jodiye jo daayen taraf \(x\)-axis ke qareeb jaye magar use na chhooye (Figure 1.7).
Kyun: curve ki shakal Steps 1-3 se tay hai.

Tasdeeq: \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{x} = 2^{-x}\), is liye \(x\) par is ki value \(2^{x}\) ki \(-x\) wali value ke barabar hai: maslan \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{-2} = 4 = 2^{2}\). Yani yeh graph \(y = 2^{x}\) ka \(y\)-axis mein aaina (mirror image) hai; isi liye jahan \(2^{x}\) chadhta hai wahan yeh utarta hai.
blocks.answer: \(f(x) = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{x}\) ka graph woh hamwar, neeche utarti curve hai jo \((-2, 4)\), \((-1, 2)\), \((0, 1)\), \((1, 0.5)\), \((2, 0.25)\) se guzarti hai; yeh \(x\)-axis ke oopar rehti hai aur \(y = 0\) is ka horizontal asymptote hai (Figure 1.7).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{-100} = 1.267 \times 10^{30}\) likhti hai. Asal mein \(2^{100} = 1.26765\ldots \times 10^{30}\), jo round karne par \(1.268 \times 10^{30}\) banta hai (kitab ne value kaati hai, round nahin ki). Table mein durust value likhi gayi hai.
Upar ke tamam key points ke saath \(f(x) = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{x}\) ka graph Figure 1.7 mein dikhaya gaya hai.

The falling curve y = (1/2) to the power x passes through the dots (minus 2, 4), (minus 1, 2), (0, 1), (1, 0.5) and (2, 0.25). blocks.text: Note kijiye ke tamam exponential functions \(f(x) = a^{x}\), \(a \in \mathbb{R}\) aur \(0 < a < 1\), ke graphs taqreeban Figure 1.7 jaise hote hain: baayen se daayen utarte hue, \((0, 1)\) se guzarte hue, aur daayen taraf \(x\)-axis se lipat te hue.

Chaliye, ab poore sabaq ko ek table mein samet lete hain. Exam se pehle sirf yeh table dekh lena kaafi revision hai. Baayen column mein woh functions hain jin ka base 1 se bara hai, aur daayen column mein woh jin ka base 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan hai. Ghaur kijiye ke pehli teen rows dono taraf bilkul same hain; farq sirf direction (chadhna ya utarna) aur asymptote ki taraf ka hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(y = 3^{x}\) aur \(y = \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x}\) ke graphs mein kya cheez same hogi aur kya ulat?
Jawab: dono ka domain, range, point \((0, 1)\) aur asymptote \(y = 0\) same hain. Lekin \(3^{x}\) chadhta hai aur \(\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x}\) utarta hai; dono ek doosre ka \(y\)-axis mein aaina hain, kyun ke \(\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x} = 3^{-x}\).

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(y = a^{x}\ (a > 0, a \ne 1)\): domain \(]-\infty, \infty[\), range \(]0, \infty[\), har jagah continuous.
2. Har real \(x\) ke liye \(a^{x} > 0\): graph \(x\)-axis ke oopar rehta hai.
3. \(y\)-intercept \((0, 1)\); \(x\)-intercept koi nahin.
4. \(a > 1\) ho to strictly increasing, \(0 < a < 1\) ho to strictly decreasing; is liye one-to-one.
5. \(y = 0\) (yani \(x\)-axis) horizontal asymptote hai.
6. Graph banane ka tareeqa: pehle properties, phir \(x = -2, \ldots, 2\) ka table, phir hamwar curve.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Curve ko \(x\)-axis se chhoo dena ya us ke paar le jana. \(a^{x}\) kabhi 0 ya negative nahin hota.
2. Asymptote ko ghalat taraf dikhana. \(a > 1\) ke liye curve baayen taraf axis ke qareeb jati hai; \(0 < a < 1\) ke liye daayen taraf.
3. Asymptote \(y = 0\) ko "vertical" line kehna (jaise kitab ke note mein chhap gaya). \(y = c\) hamesha horizontal line hai.
4. Decimal ko round karne ki bajaye kaat dena: \(e^{-1} \approx 0.368\), 0.367 nahin.
